title: Read a CI pipeline file
summary: GitLab CI/CD reads jobs from its pipeline configuration. A job names commands for a runner, which is the worker that executes them.
introduction: GitLab CI/CD reads jobs from its pipeline configuration. A job names commands for a runner, which is the worker that executes them. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain read a ci pipeline file
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: GitLab CI/CD reads jobs from its pipeline configuration. A job names commands for a runner, which is the worker that executes them.

blocks.code:
File: .gitlab-ci.yml
Job name: test
Stage: test
Script: npm test
blocks.title: Read a CI pipeline file

blocks.text: This is a worked description of a job, not executable YAML. The runner needs a suitable environment with the project dependencies installed.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Name one thing a runner needs before it can run npm test.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A job name such as test does not prove meaningful tests were configured.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).
